ledger.claim: The 5.00 SGD in issue is not on the rider today. The payments ledger records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00 after the rider's complaint, and the filing party is the DRIVER, so the only way the rider ends up carrying the disputed charge is a ruling that moves it back onto him. Under POL-GEN-03 a ruling of NO_ACTION preserves the present state and 'never means restore a charge'. The rider's case is therefore put on this trip's own evidence and on the clause that governs it, not on the platform's no-show automation.

POL-NS-21 gives the rider of a scheduled trip whose driver arrives early the full free wait measured from the scheduled pickup time, so the protected window on this booking ran from 07:45:00 to 07:50:00 - exactly what the trip record's own derived free_wait block states (starts_from scheduled_at, starts_at 07:45:00, ends_at 07:50:00, free_wait_sec 300). The platform's wait timer on this trip nevertheless started at 07:39:35, on the driver's early arrival, and expired at 07:44:35 - before the rider's booked pickup time. The no-show here was therefore processed on a start POL-NS-21 does not authorise, and the 'wait_timer_expired' event at 07:44:35 cannot itself carry the charge. The rider states plainly that the derivation puts the corrected deadline at 07:50:00 and that the 07:51:40 cancellation falls after it; his point is that the 5.00 was produced by the platform's timer and not by the clause.

The rider does not contend that POL-NS-23's contact obligation was breached, and says so rather than stretching it. The chat log carries two in-app messages from the driver, at 07:40:00 (read by the rider at 07:40:22) and 07:46:20 (read at 07:46:30), and the trip record's in_app_calls carries two calls placed by the driver at 07:47:30 and 07:50:10 - all four before the 07:51:40 cancellation - with the derived contact_before_cancel block recording obligation_met as true. That route to voiding the fee is closed on this record.

POL-NS-24 is not engaged either, and the rider concedes it. The driver reached the pickup at 07:39:30, corroborated by the GPS trace within the 50 m STANDARD-zone arrival radius (nearest fix 1.758 m from the pickup at 07:40:40, accuracy 3.0 m), well before the scheduled time plus five minutes (07:50:00). The rider thus had no no-charge cancellation right on this trip, and the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not arise, because it additionally requires that the driver failed to attempt contact and the record shows two messages and two calls.

ledger.claim: The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is fully met. Before cancelling at 07:51:40 the driver sent two in-app chat messages (07:40:00, read by the rider at 07:40:22; 07:46:20, read at 07:46:30) and placed two in-app calls (07:47:30, ringing 28 s; 07:50:10, ringing 20 s) — all before trip_record.cancelled_at. The clause requires that a message and a call be placed, not answered, and the derived contact block confirms obligation_met = true with 2 messages and 2 calls. Nothing in the contact test is missing, so the fee is not voided.

The driver was entitled to cancel as a no-show at 07:51:40. Under POL-NS-21, for a scheduled trip where the driver arrived before the scheduled time, the 300 s free wait runs from the scheduled pickup at 07:45:00 and ends at 07:50:00. The driver arrived at 07:39:30, so the free wait had expired before the cancellation, and the derived free_wait block records cancelled_after_free_wait = true. The same conclusion follows on the platform's own timer, which expired even earlier at 07:44:35.

The arrival is corroborated on the trace, so it is not merely a self-report. The GPS arrival test returns corroborated = true: the nearest fix sits 1.758 m from the pickup point at 07:40:40 with a reported accuracy of 3 m (inside the 25 m accuracy filter and well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for this STANDARD zone pickup), and the driver's fixes then stay stationary at the pickup from 07:39:40 through 07:51:40 — a dwell of about twelve minutes at the kerb.

The rider's complaint gives no route to a refund under POL-NS-24. That clause refunds the fee only where the driver failed to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, i.e. 07:50:00. The record shows arrival at 07:39:30 — before the 07:45 schedule and more than ten minutes ahead of the deadline — and the derived driver_deadline block sets arrived_by_deadline = true. Being early is not a ground the clause recognises: the free wait is fixed to the scheduled time, so an early arrival lengthened the rider's window rather than shortening it, and no goodwill credit arises because contact was attempted.

The rider was not at the pickup during the wait on his own account. His counterparty statement places him coming down at 07:53 — three minutes after the free wait closed at 07:50:00 and more than a minute after the 07:51:40 cancellation. Both of the driver's messages carry read receipts (07:40:22 and 07:46:30), so the rider knew a vehicle was waiting and did not descend within the window; the trace carries no rider track at all, so nothing in the record puts him at the kerb before the cancellation.

The fee charged is exactly the policy fee and belongs to the driver. POL-NS-22 fixes the no-show fee at 5.00 SGD, and the payments ledger shows cancellation_fee 5.00 SGD with fee_matches_policy = true and driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd = 5.00. Because the free-wait and contact conditions are satisfied, the fee stands and the ruling should be DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to 5.00 SGD.

No_ACTION cannot be the outcome here because the present state is adverse to the driver. The interim reversal that followed the rider's complaint has already moved the money: payment_status is REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd is 5.00, and the trip record shows the sum withheld from the driver pending review. POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative — it preserves the present payment state — so it would leave the rider refunded and the driver unpaid on a fee he earned. DRIVER_COMPENSATION is the only value that restores the 5.00 SGD to the driver.

The missing traffic advisory is disclosed rather than relied on: EV-ADVIS-05058-01 is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, so it carries no fact. Its absence opens no question under POL-GEN-26, because no element of the no-show test — arrival, free wait, or contact — depends on a traffic advisory, and each of those elements is carried by a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0 (the trip record, the chat log and the GPS trace).

The AI ruling is final on this dispute and no escalation is engaged. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries fraud_flags of 1 or more, so the 0.95 bar does not apply; and the record carries no safety indicator, so POL-GEN-21 is not triggered. POL-NS-26 confirms that the ruling on a no-show is final with the fee fixed at 5.00 SGD.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this is the 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee on trip TRP-05058 (POLICY-NO-SHOW v7.0.0). The fee is upheld and the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, moving 5.00 SGD to the driver D-24128.

WHY THE NO-SHOW STANDS. The pickup was booked for 07:45. The driver reached the pickup at 07:39:30 — before the scheduled time — so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait ran from the scheduled pickup, 07:45:00, and closed at 07:50:00. He cancelled at 07:51:40, after that deadline. The trip record's own derivations (EV-TRIP-05058, weight 1.0) set the same figures: free_wait starts_from scheduled_at, 07:45:00 to 07:50:00, cancelled_after_free_wait true, arrived_by_deadline true. An early arrival lengthens the rider's protected window rather than shortening it.

Rider, your specific point — that the platform's timer started at the driver's early arrival (07:39:35) and expired at 07:44:35, before your booked time — is correct as far as it goes, and that 'wait_timer_expired' event cannot by itself carry the charge (POL-NS-21). It does not help you here: on the clause-corrected deadline of 07:50:00 the cancellation at 07:51:40 is still late, so the fee rests on the clause, not on the automation.

The arrival is corroborated on the GPS trace (EV-GPS-05058, weight 1.0): the nearest fix sits 1.758 m from the pickup at 07:40:40 with 3.0 m reported accuracy, inside the 25 m accuracy filter and the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the vehicle is stationary at the kerb from 07:39:40 to 07:51:40.

The contact obligation in POL-NS-23 is met: two in-app messages (07:40:00, read 07:40:22; 07:46:20, read 07:46:30) and two in-app calls (07:47:30 ringing 28 s; 07:50:10 ringing 20 s), all before the 07:51:40 cancellation (EV-CHAT-05058 and EV-TRIP-05058, both weight 1.0). That route to voiding the fee is closed, and the rider's advocate correctly conceded it.

POL-NS-24 is not engaged: the driver arrived at 07:39:30, more than ten minutes before the 07:50:00 deadline, so no refund of the fee is owed and the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not arise, contact having been attempted in any case. Your own account in your counterparty statement — that you came down at 07:53 — places you at the pickup after both the close of the free wait (07:50:00) and the cancellation (07:51:40).

WHY THE MONEY MOVES TO THE DRIVER. The payments ledger (EV-FARE-05058, weight 1.0) records cancellation_fee 5.00 SGD and fee_matches_policy true, with refund_issued_sgd 5.00 after your complaint. POL-NS-22 fixes the no-show fee at 5.00 SGD and transfers it to the driver as compensation for time and fuel. The interim reversal means the present state is adverse to the filing driver, and POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative — it preserves the present state and never restores a charge — so NO_ACTION would leave the driver unpaid on a fee he earned. DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00 SGD is the value that moves the money.

NO REFERRALS. Because the amount charged equals the policy fee of 5.00 SGD, POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not fire. POL-NS-25 does not fire: the rider's 30-day no-show counter is not present on the profile snapshot, and that clause applies only when the field is present and is 3 or more. POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not fire, as the driver arrived by the deadline.

NO ESCALATION. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so the 0.95 bar is not raised and the ruling is final under POL-NS-26. Nothing in the record raises a POL-GEN-21 safety indicator. The only impaired artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05058-01 (MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), carries no fact and no element of the no-show test depends on it, so it opens no question under POL-GEN-26.

CONFIDENCE. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact — the trip record, the chat log and the GPS trace — sits at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the cap is 1.0; confidence is stated at 0.93.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
